links.outcome: Open-ended CKD medication review performance versus multiple-choice benchmark expectations
links.effect: Macro F1 ranged 0.41 to 0.49; open-ended scoring exposed LLM failures invisible to multiple-choice benchmarks, so generic benchmarks overstate competence.
links.quote: This nephrology-specific benchmark exposes clinically important LLM blind spots that generic multiple-choice evaluations would not detect.

links.outcome: Fabricated dose caps in LLM medication review outputs
links.effect: PI-adjudicated hallucination ranged from 0% (GPT-5.4) to 54% (DeepSeek R1), including fabricated dose caps.
links.quote: PI-adjudicated hallucination ranged from 0% (GPT-5.4) to 54% (DeepSeek R1), including fabricated dose caps and non-existent guideline citations.

links.outcome: Non-existent guideline citations in LLM outputs
links.effect: Hallucination up to 54% (DeepSeek R1), including non-existent guideline citations.

links.outcome: Detection of clinically important drug-related problems and omissions in medication review
links.effect: Safety-critical omission rate 22% to 48%; phosphate binder timing detected 11% and hyperkalemia combinations 33%.
links.quote: Phosphate binder timing (11%) and hyperkalemia combinations (33%) were poorly detected across all models.

screen.reason: Evaluates frontier LLMs on a synthetic, trap-embedded benchmark for nephrology medication review without testing an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
